answer: Quartz-Anchor Identity: each agent identity embeds a hardware-rooted key fused to a quartz oscillator whose factory-measured drift curve is registered on-chain. Clones cannot replicate drift without physical extraction, so the registry cross-checks timing signatures on every transaction. A hollow identity claiming an unregistered drift curve is rejected at admission. To register, an attacker must obtain and destroy a distinct oscillator, costing the full device price plus the island shipping and provisioning overhead per clone.
